title: You Now Own Team Performance
lesson_text: You are responsible for team performance—not just activity.
action_text: Before mid-day, do this: 1.Pull yesterday’s performance (CSAT, QA, AHT, etc.) 2.Identify: •1 top performer •1 average performer •1 struggling performer 3.Write ONE reason for each Say This (to leadership or yourself): “My team’s performance breaks down like this…” Do: Look for patterns Don’t: Say “everyone is doing fine”
reflection_question: Can you clearly explain your team’s performance without guessing? ⸻

title: You Now Own Team Performance
lesson_text: If “good” isn’t defined, performance will be inconsistent.
action_text: Pick ONE behavior (example: call opening) Say to team: “Here’s what good looks like starting today: [Specific behavior — ex: greeting, tone, confidence]. This is the expectation every time.” Do: Be specific Don’t: Say “just improve your calls”
reflection_question: Would a new employee understand exactly what to do? ⸻

title: You Now Own Team Performance
lesson_text: Jumping in too quickly prevents team growth.
action_text: When someone struggles: Ask: “What do you think the next step is?” Wait. Let them answer. Then guide—not take over. Do: Let them think Don’t: Jump in and fix it immediately
reflection_question: Did you develop them—or rescue them? ⸻

title: You Now Own Team Performance
lesson_text: Your emotional control sets the tone for the entire team.
action_text: Today, control: •Voice (steady, not reactive) •Speed (don’t rush decisions) •Language (clear, not scattered) Say This in pressure: “Let’s slow this down—here’s what we’re going to do.” Do: Create calm Don’t: react emotionally
reflection_question: Did your presence stabilize or stress the team? ⸻

title: You Now Own Team Performance
lesson_text: Supervisors own outcomes—even when they didn’t cause them.
action_text: When something goes wrong: Say: “That’s on me—I’ll make sure we correct it.” Do: Own it publicly Don’t: Blame the rep
reflection_question: Did you take responsibility or shift it? ⸻ 🔥 SUPERVISOR — WEEK 2 (REBUILT ELITE) Theme: Setting & Enforcing Standards ⸻

title: Setting & Enforcing Standards
lesson_text: Standards must be seen and heard daily—not just documented.
action_text: Today, do this 3 times: •Observe behavior •Call it out immediately (good or bad) Say This: “That’s exactly what we’re looking for—keep doing that.” OR “That’s not the standard—here’s what we need instead…” Do: Address in the moment Don’t: Wait until end of day
reflection_question: Did your team hear the standard today? ⸻

title: Setting & Enforcing Standards
lesson_text: Inconsistent enforcement destroys credibility.
action_text: Today: •Correct a top performer if needed •Correct a low performer the same way Say This: “We’re holding the same standard across the team.” Do: Be consistent Don’t: give passes to high performers
reflection_question: Did you treat everyone equally? ⸻

title: Setting & Enforcing Standards
lesson_text: Vague feedback leads to no improvement.
action_text: Instead of saying: “Do better” Say: “On your last interaction, you missed [specific behavior]. Next time, do this instead: [specific action].” Do: Be exact Don’t: generalize feedback
reflection_question: Could they repeat the behavior correctly next time? ⸻

title: Setting & Enforcing Standards
lesson_text: Repetition builds discipline.
action_text: Pick ONE focus today (example: tone) Reinforce it: •in team huddle •during live observation •during coaching Say This each time: “Remember—this is the standard.” Do: Repeat often Don’t: assume one mention is enough
reflection_question: Did repetition improve consistency? ⸻

title: Setting & Enforcing Standards
lesson_text: If you don’t hold the line, the line moves.
action_text: Today: •Address something you normally let slide Say: “We can’t allow that moving forward—here’s the expectation.” Do: Correct immediately Don’t: ignore small issues
reflection_question: Did you protect the standard—or lower it? ⸻ 🔥 SUPERVISOR — WEEK 3 (REBUILT ELITE) Theme: Managing Performance Across the Entire Team (Not Just Individuals) ⸻

title: Managing Performance Across the Entire Team (Not Just Individuals)
lesson_text: If you only focus on 1–2 people, you’re not managing the team—you’re reacting.
action_text: Today, do this: 1.Look at your full team list 2.Label each person: •Green = strong •Yellow = average •Red = struggling 3.Count how many are in each category Say This (to yourself or leadership): “My team is trending: X strong, X average, X struggling.” Do: Look at the whole team Don’t: focus only on top/bottom performers
reflection_question: Did you evaluate your entire team or just a few people? ⸻

title: Managing Performance Across the Entire Team (Not Just Individuals)
lesson_text: Average performers determine your team’s overall success.
action_text: Pick ONE “average” (yellow) employee today. Say: “You’re doing solid—but here’s what will take you to the next level: [specific behavior].” Do: develop the middle Don’t: ignore them because they’re “fine”
reflection_question: Did you elevate someone who usually gets overlooked? ⸻

title: Managing Performance Across the Entire Team (Not Just Individuals)
lesson_text: Patterns matter more than one-off mistakes.
action_text: Today, track ONE repeated issue across at least 3 reps (example: weak call closing, tone, missed steps) Write it down. Say This in team setting: “I’m noticing a pattern—we need to fix this across the board…” Do: coach patterns Don’t: treat everything as isolated
reflection_question: Did you identify a real team-wide issue? ⸻

title: Managing Performance Across the Entire Team (Not Just Individuals)
lesson_text: Team performance improves when you fix shared problems.
action_text: Address your identified pattern with the full team. Say: “Here’s what I’m seeing—and here’s how we fix it: [clear behavior].” Do: coach the group Don’t: repeat the same 1:1 conversation 10 times
reflection_question: Did your coaching reach multiple people at once? ⸻

title: Managing Performance Across the Entire Team (Not Just Individuals)
lesson_text: Supervisors improve performance at scale—not one person at a time.
action_text: Implement ONE change today that impacts everyone (example: new call flow expectation, tone standard) Say This: “Starting today, this is how we’re doing this moving forward…” Do: make team-wide adjustments Don’t: rely only on individual fixes
reflection_question: Did your action improve the entire team? ⸻ 🔥 SUPERVISOR — WEEK 4 (REBUILT ELITE) Theme: Coaching Multiple People Effectively (Without Burning Out) ⸻

title: Coaching Multiple People Effectively (Without Burning Out)
lesson_text: If you coach one person at a time all day—you will fall behind.
action_text: Identify ONE issue affecting multiple reps. Coach it once to the group. Say This: “I’m going to coach this once for everyone—listen up…” Do: coach in batches Don’t: repeat the same coaching 5+ times individually
reflection_question: Did you save time while increasing impact? ⸻

title: Coaching Multiple People Effectively (Without Burning Out)
lesson_text: Supervisors must coach in real-time—not just scheduled sessions.
action_text: During live work: •Observe behavior •Immediately step in after Say: “Quick coaching moment—next time, say it like this…” Do: coach immediately Don’t: wait until later
reflection_question: Did timing improve the learning? ⸻

title: Coaching Multiple People Effectively (Without Burning Out)
lesson_text: People remember what they see more than what they’re told.
action_text: Demonstrate the correct behavior. Say: “Here’s exactly how that should sound…” Then model it. Do: show, not just tell Don’t: explain without demonstration
reflection_question: Did modeling improve understanding? ⸻

title: Coaching Multiple People Effectively (Without Burning Out)
lesson_text: Coaching must include follow-up—or it doesn’t stick.
action_text: Revisit someone you coached earlier. Say: “Let me hear how you’re doing it now.” Do: check for improvement Don’t: assume they fixed it
reflection_question: Did you confirm behavior changed? ⸻

title: Coaching Multiple People Effectively (Without Burning Out)
lesson_text: Your goal is not to correct—it’s to build capability.
action_text: Instead of fixing: Ask: “What would you do differently next time?” Let them answer first. Do: build thinking Don’t: give every answer
reflection_question: Did they learn—or just follow instructions? ⸻ 🔥 WHAT YOU JUST BUILT This is now: ✔ team-level performance management ✔ pattern-based coaching system ✔ time-efficient supervisor workflow ✔ real-world application training ⸻ SUPERVISOR — WEEK 5 (REBUILT ELITE) Theme: Accountability Conversations That Actually Work ⸻

title: Accountability Conversations That Actually Work
lesson_text: If you delay accountability, the behavior becomes the standard.
action_text: When you see a miss today, address it within 5 minutes. Say: “I want to address something quickly—on that last interaction, you missed [specific behavior].” Pause. “Moving forward, here’s what I expect instead: [specific action].” Do: address it immediately Don’t: wait until end of shift
reflection_question: Did you correct the behavior in real time? ⸻

title: Accountability Conversations That Actually Work
lesson_text: Vague accountability creates repeat mistakes.
action_text: Replace general feedback with exact language. Instead of: “Be better with customers” Say: “When the customer pushed back, you skipped acknowledging them. Next time say: ‘I understand how that feels…’ before responding.” Do: be exact Don’t: generalize feedback
reflection_question: Could they repeat the correct behavior immediately? ⸻

title: Accountability Conversations That Actually Work
lesson_text: Your tone determines whether the message is accepted or resisted.
action_text: Deliver accountability with: •calm tone •neutral facial expression •controlled pace Say: “This isn’t a big issue—but it is important to fix.” Do: stay composed Don’t: sound frustrated or emotional
reflection_question: Did your tone help or hurt the message? ⸻

title: Accountability Conversations That Actually Work
lesson_text: Top performers must still be held accountable.
action_text: Correct a strong performer today if needed. Say: “I know you’re one of our stronger reps—that’s exactly why I’m holding you to this standard.” Do: hold everyone accountable Don’t: give passes to high performers
reflection_question: Did you stay consistent across the team? ⸻

title: Accountability Conversations That Actually Work
lesson_text: Accountability without follow-up is ineffective.
action_text: Revisit a correction from earlier. Say: “Earlier we talked about [behavior]—let me hear how you’re doing it now.” Do: verify improvement Don’t: assume it’s fixed
reflection_question: Did the behavior actually improve? ⸻ 🔥 SUPERVISOR — WEEK 6 (REBUILT ELITE) Theme: Time & Priority Management (Stop Reacting, Start Leading) ⸻

title: Time & Priority Management (Stop Reacting, Start Leading)
lesson_text: If you start your day reacting, you’ll stay reactive all day.
action_text: Before your shift starts: 1.Review team performance 2.Identify 2 priorities (ex: coaching, quality, escalations) 3.Write them down Say to yourself: “If I only accomplish these 2 things today, it’s a successful day.” Do: set priorities early Don’t: jump straight into reacting
reflection_question: Did you lead your day—or react to it? ⸻

title: Time & Priority Management (Stop Reacting, Start Leading)
lesson_text: Supervisors fail when they do work their team should handle.
action_text: When something comes to you: Ask: “Is this something they can handle with guidance?” If YES → coach, don’t take over Say: “Walk me through how you would handle this.” Do: delegate thinking Don’t: solve everything yourself
reflection_question: Did you lead—or do the work for them? ⸻

title: Time & Priority Management (Stop Reacting, Start Leading)
lesson_text: Interruptions will control your day if you let them.
action_text: When multiple issues hit: Say: “One at a time—here’s the order we’re handling this…” Then prioritize: 1.urgent 2.important 3.can wait Do: control flow Don’t: react to everything at once
reflection_question: Did you create order or chaos? ⸻

title: Time & Priority Management (Stop Reacting, Start Leading)
lesson_text: If you don’t schedule coaching, it won’t happen.
action_text: Block 20–30 minutes today for coaching. Say to team: “During this time, I’ll be focused on coaching and development.” Do: protect coaching time Don’t: skip it for “busyness”
reflection_question: Did you invest time in development? ⸻

title: Time & Priority Management (Stop Reacting, Start Leading)
lesson_text: Your priorities determine your team’s results.
action_text: Before ending your day, ask: •Did I coach someone? •Did I improve team performance? •Did I enforce a standard? Say: “This is what moved the team forward today…” Do: measure your impact Don’t: end the day without reflection
reflection_question: Did your actions actually improve the team? SUPERVISOR — WEEK 7 Theme: Decision-Making Under Pressure ⸻

title: Decision-Making Under Pressure
lesson_text: Indecision creates confusion faster than a wrong decision.
action_text: When an issue comes up: 1.Define the issue 2.Pick the best option quickly 3.Communicate clearly Say: “Here’s what we’re doing—this is the direction.” Do: decide clearly Don’t: say “I’m not sure…”
reflection_question: Did your decision create movement or delay? ⸻

title: Decision-Making Under Pressure
lesson_text: Your team needs direction—not options.
action_text: When asked what to do: Don’t say: “What do you think?” Instead say: “Here’s the approach—let’s execute this.” Do: lead decisions Don’t: push decisions back
reflection_question: Did you provide direction or confusion? ⸻

title: Decision-Making Under Pressure
lesson_text: Pressure tests your leadership—not your knowledge.
action_text: When things get busy: Slow your response. Say: “Let’s take this one step at a time.” Do: control pace Don’t: rush decisions
reflection_question: Did you stay in control? ⸻

title: Decision-Making Under Pressure
lesson_text: Supervisors must commit to decisions.
action_text: After making a decision: Stand by it unless clearly wrong. Say: “This is the direction we’re going—stick with it.” Do: commit Don’t: flip decisions constantly
reflection_question: Did you stay consistent? ⸻

title: Decision-Making Under Pressure
lesson_text: Clear decisions build trust fast.
action_text: End every decision with clarity: “Here’s the next step.” Do: close the loop Don’t: leave things open-ended
reflection_question: Did your team know exactly what to do next? ⸻ 🔥 SUPERVISOR — WEEK 8 Theme: Handling Escalations Like a Leader ⸻

title: Handling Escalations Like a Leader
lesson_text: Escalations are leadership moments—not interruptions.
action_text: When escalation happens: Say: “I’ve got this—let’s walk through it.” Do: step in confidently Don’t: hesitate
reflection_question: Did you take control quickly? ⸻

title: Handling Escalations Like a Leader
lesson_text: Customers want confidence—not complexity.
action_text: Say: “I understand the concern. Here’s what I’m going to do to resolve this…” Then outline steps. Do: lead solution Don’t: over-explain
reflection_question: Did you simplify the situation? ⸻

title: Handling Escalations Like a Leader
lesson_text: Your tone can calm or escalate the situation.
action_text: Lower your tone + slow your speech. Say: “I hear you—we’re going to resolve this.” Do: stay calm Don’t: match frustration
reflection_question: Did your tone reduce tension? ⸻

title: Handling Escalations Like a Leader
lesson_text: Your team is watching how you handle pressure.
action_text: Narrate your process: “Here’s what I’m doing now…” Do: model behavior Don’t: disappear into the issue
reflection_question: Did your team learn from you? ⸻

title: Handling Escalations Like a Leader
lesson_text: Escalations should end with clarity.
action_text: Close with: “Here’s what will happen next and when.” Do: give timeline Don’t: leave uncertainty
reflection_question: Did you fully close the situation? ⸻ 🔥 SUPERVISOR — WEEK 9 Theme: Fixing Underperformance (Step-by-Step) ⸻

title: Fixing Underperformance (Step-by-Step)
lesson_text: Underperformance ignored becomes culture.
action_text: Identify 1 struggling rep. Say: “I want to work with you to improve this specific area…” Do: address early Don’t: wait
reflection_question: Did you take action immediately? ⸻

title: Fixing Underperformance (Step-by-Step)
lesson_text: You must define the problem clearly.
action_text: Say: “Here’s exactly where you’re missing the mark: [specific behavior]” Do: be specific Don’t: generalize
reflection_question: Did they understand the issue? ⸻

title: Fixing Underperformance (Step-by-Step)
lesson_text: Improvement requires a plan.
action_text: Create a simple plan: •what to fix •how to fix it •when to review Say: “Here’s what we’re going to focus on this week…”
reflection_question: Did you give direction? ⸻

title: Fixing Underperformance (Step-by-Step)
lesson_text: Follow-up is everything.
action_text: Revisit within 24–48 hours. Say: “Let’s review your progress.”
reflection_question: Did you follow through? ⸻

title: Fixing Underperformance (Step-by-Step)
lesson_text: Consistency fixes performance—not one conversation.
action_text: Track improvement daily.
reflection_question: Did behavior change over time? ⸻ 🔥 SUPERVISOR — WEEK 10 Theme: Running a High-Performing Shift ⸻

title: Running a High-Performing Shift (Full Control)
lesson_text: If you don’t set the tone at the start, the team will.
action_text: Before work begins: Say: “Team—today we are focused on 2 things: 1.[example: call control] 2.[example: tone consistency] This is what good looks like…” Then define ONE behavior. Do: set focus early Don’t: start without direction
reflection_question: Did you begin the shift with clear priorities?

title: Running a High-Performing Shift (Full Control)
lesson_text: Performance drops when there’s no reset.
action_text: Halfway through shift: Say: “Quick reset—here’s where we need to tighten up: [specific issue]. Let’s refocus for the next block.” Do: reset performance Don’t: let drift continue
reflection_question: Did the mid-shift reset improve focus?

title: Running a High-Performing Shift (Full Control)
lesson_text: Supervisors must stay visible to stay effective.
action_text: Every hour: •walk the floor •listen to 1–2 interactions •give 1 coaching moment Say: “Quick feedback—here’s one thing to adjust…” Do: stay present Don’t: sit behind a desk all day
reflection_question: Did your visibility improve team performance?

title: Running a High-Performing Shift (Full Control)
lesson_text: Energy drops = performance drops.
action_text: When team slows down: Say: “Let’s lock in for the next 30 minutes—this is where we finish strong.” Do: re-engage team Don’t: ignore low energy
reflection_question: Did you successfully re-engage the team?

title: Running a High-Performing Shift (Full Control)
lesson_text: Strong leaders close the day with clarity.
action_text: Say: “Here’s what we did well today: [1–2 things] Here’s what we fix tomorrow: [1 focus area]” Do: close with direction Don’t: end without feedback
reflection_question: Did your closing create clarity for tomorrow?

title: Advanced Accountability (When Behavior Repeats)
lesson_text: Repeated issues require a stronger conversation—not the same one.
action_text: Say: “This has come up more than once—so we need to address it directly.” Do: escalate seriousness Don’t: repeat soft coaching
reflection_question: Did your message reflect urgency? ⸻

title: Advanced Accountability (When Behavior Repeats)
lesson_text: You must separate behavior from the person.
action_text: Say: “This is about the behavior—not you. Here’s what needs to change…” Do: stay professional Don’t: make it personal
reflection_question: Did you stay focused on behavior? ⸻

title: Advanced Accountability (When Behavior Repeats)
lesson_text: Consequences must be clear—even if not enforced immediately.
action_text: Say: “If this continues, it will lead to [clear next step].” Do: set expectations Don’t: threaten vaguely
reflection_question: Did they understand the stakes? ⸻

title: Advanced Accountability (When Behavior Repeats)
lesson_text: Silence after accountability creates confusion.
action_text: Ask: “Walk me through how you’ll handle this next time.” Do: confirm understanding Don’t: assume it
reflection_question: Did they clearly explain the fix? ⸻

title: Advanced Accountability (When Behavior Repeats)
lesson_text: Accountability must be followed quickly.
action_text: Check back next shift. Say: “I want to see how you’re applying what we discussed.”
reflection_question: Did behavior improve? ⸻ 🔥 SUPERVISOR — WEEK 12 (ELITE) Theme: Coaching That Actually Changes Behavior ⸻

title: Coaching That Actually Changes Behavior
lesson_text: Telling someone what to do is not coaching.
action_text: Say: “Here’s how it should sound…” Demonstrate → then say: “Now you try it.” Do: practice live Don’t: just explain
reflection_question: Did they perform it correctly? ⸻

title: Coaching That Actually Changes Behavior
lesson_text: Immediate correction is more effective than delayed feedback.
action_text: After interaction: Say: “Pause—next time say it like this…” Do: coach immediately Don’t: wait
reflection_question: Did timing improve learning? ⸻

title: Coaching That Actually Changes Behavior
lesson_text: Repetition builds confidence.
action_text: Have them repeat the corrected behavior 2–3 times. Do: reinforce Don’t: move on too quickly
reflection_question: Did repetition improve execution? ⸻

title: Coaching That Actually Changes Behavior
lesson_text: Recognition locks in behavior.
action_text: Say: “That’s exactly it—keep doing that.” Do: reinforce success Don’t: only focus on mistakes
reflection_question: Did they gain confidence? ⸻

title: Coaching That Actually Changes Behavior
lesson_text: Coaching must be tracked to matter.
action_text: Write down: •who you coached •what behavior •next follow-up
reflection_question: Are you tracking improvement—or guessing? ⸻ 🔥 SUPERVISOR — WEEK 13 (ELITE) Theme: Managing Team Energy & Morale (Without Losing Control) ⸻

title: Managing Team Energy & Morale (Without Losing Control)
lesson_text: Low energy spreads faster than high energy.
action_text: Call it out early: Say: “Energy feels low—let’s reset and refocus.”
reflection_question: Did you address it early? ⸻

title: Managing Team Energy & Morale (Without Losing Control)
lesson_text: Recognition drives engagement.
action_text: Call out one rep publicly: “Great job handling that call—exactly what we need.”
reflection_question: Did recognition lift the team? ⸻

title: Managing Team Energy & Morale (Without Losing Control)
lesson_text: Negativity must be corrected immediately.
action_text: Say privately: “That energy doesn’t work for the team—let’s reset.”
reflection_question: Did you correct it quickly? ⸻

title: Managing Team Energy & Morale (Without Losing Control)
lesson_text: Morale improves when direction is clear.
action_text: Say: “Here’s our focus—let’s lock in.”
reflection_question: Did clarity improve engagement? ⸻

title: Managing Team Energy & Morale (Without Losing Control)
lesson_text: You control the emotional tone of the team.
action_text: Maintain calm + confident behavior all day.
reflection_question: Did your presence influence morale? ⸻ 🔥 SUPERVISOR — WEEK 14 (ELITE) Theme: Owning Metrics (CSAT / QA / AHT) ⸻

title: Owning Metrics (CSAT / QA / AHT)
lesson_text: Metrics reflect behavior—not luck.
action_text: Pick ONE metric. Say: “This number is driven by this behavior: [specific].”
reflection_question: Did you connect behavior to metrics? ⸻

title: Owning Metrics (CSAT / QA / AHT)
lesson_text: You must coach to drivers—not numbers.
action_text: Say: “To improve this, we need to fix this behavior…”
reflection_question: Did you coach correctly? ⸻

title: Owning Metrics (CSAT / QA / AHT)
lesson_text: Teams perform better when they see results.
action_text: Share numbers: “Here’s where we stand today…”
reflection_question: Did visibility improve accountability? ⸻

title: Owning Metrics (CSAT / QA / AHT)
lesson_text: Daily adjustments improve metrics faster.
action_text: Make ONE change today.
reflection_question: Did it impact performance? ⸻

title: Owning Metrics (CSAT / QA / AHT)
lesson_text: Supervisors own the number—period.
action_text: Say: “This result is on me—we’re fixing it.”
reflection_question: Did you take ownership? ⸻ 🔥 SUPERVISOR — WEEK 15 (ELITE) Theme: Becoming the Leader People Follow ⸻

title: Becoming the Leader People Follow
lesson_text: Consistency builds credibility.
action_text: Maintain same tone + standards all day. ⸻
reflection_question: Were your tone and standards consistent all day?

title: Becoming the Leader People Follow
lesson_text: Clear communication builds trust.
action_text: Speak directly and confidently. ⸻
reflection_question: Did your communication build trust?

title: Becoming the Leader People Follow
lesson_text: Visibility builds influence.
action_text: Stay present on the floor. ⸻
reflection_question: Did your presence strengthen your influence?

title: Becoming the Leader People Follow
lesson_text: Leaders step in when it matters most.
action_text: Take control in a key moment. ⸻
reflection_question: Did you step in effectively when it mattered?

title: Becoming the Leader People Follow
lesson_text: Leadership is proven daily.
action_text: Operate at your highest level all day. (How to run a team daily without failing” 10-15) ⸻ 🔥 SUPERVISOR — WEEK 16 Theme: Identifying & Developing Future Leaders ⸻
reflection_question: Did you operate at your highest leadership level today?

title: Identifying & Developing Future Leaders
lesson_text: Not every employee should be developed the same—leaders are identified, not assumed.
action_text: Review your team Identify 1 person who: takes initiative communicates well influences others Write their name down ⸻ Say This “I’ve been watching your work—you show signs of leadership. I’m going to start developing you differently.” ⸻ Do: be intentional Don’t: treat everyone the same ⸻
reflection_question: Did you identify a team member with leadership potential?

title: Identifying & Developing Future Leaders
lesson_text: Future leaders must think independently—not depend on you.
action_text: When they ask for help: Pause and say: “What do you think the best move is?” Let them answer FIRST. ⸻ Do: build thinking Don’t: give immediate answers ⸻
reflection_question: Did your question encourage independent thinking?

title: Identifying & Developing Future Leaders
lesson_text: Leadership is built through responsibility, not observation.
action_text: Assign a leadership task: “Run the next team reset or huddle.” ⸻ Do: give real responsibility Don’t: keep control of everything ⸻
reflection_question: Did the leadership task build their confidence?

title: Identifying & Developing Future Leaders
lesson_text: High performers need higher expectations to grow.
action_text: Say: “I’m holding you to a higher standard because you’re capable of more.” ⸻ Do: raise expectations Don’t: keep standards equal ⸻
reflection_question: Did the higher standard encourage growth?

title: Identifying & Developing Future Leaders
lesson_text: Your leadership impact is measured by who you develop.
action_text: Spend 15 minutes coaching them on decision-making. ⸻ Do: invest intentionally Don’t: assume growth happens naturally ⸻
reflection_question: Did your coaching strengthen their decision-making?

title: Running High-Impact 1:1s
lesson_text: Unstructured 1:1s waste time and create no change.
action_text: Structure every 1:1: Performance Behavior Next focus ⸻ Say This “Let’s walk through your performance, then one thing we’re improving this week.” ⸻ Do: follow structure Don’t: “just talk” ⸻
reflection_question: Did the structure make the one-on-one more effective?

title: Running High-Impact 1:1s
lesson_text: Clarity at the end drives improvement.
action_text: End with ONE focus. ⸻ Say This “Your focus this week is: [specific behavior].” ⸻ Do: give one priority Don’t: overload ⸻
reflection_question: Did they leave with one clear focus?

title: Running High-Impact 1:1s
lesson_text: Listening builds trust—and reveals issues faster.
action_text: Ask: “What’s been challenging for you recently?” Listen fully. ⸻ Do: listen without interrupting Don’t: rush to fix ⸻
reflection_question: Did listening reveal an important issue?

title: Running High-Impact 1:1s
lesson_text: If it’s not documented, it didn’t happen.
action_text: Write: issue expectation follow-up date ⸻ Do: document Don’t: rely on memory ⸻
reflection_question: Did your documentation create clear accountability?

title: Running High-Impact 1:1s
lesson_text: Follow-up is where real change happens.
action_text: Say: “We’ll revisit this next week.” ⸻ Do: set follow-up Don’t: leave it open ⸻
reflection_question: Did you establish a clear follow-up commitment?

title: Escalation Systems (Control at Scale)
lesson_text: Escalations without structure create chaos.
action_text: Define process: Assess Respond Resolve ⸻ Say This “Here’s how we handle escalations moving forward…” ⸻ Do: standardize Don’t: react randomly ⸻
reflection_question: Did the structure make the escalation easier to manage?

title: Escalation Systems (Control at Scale)
lesson_text: Recurring escalations reveal deeper problems.
